purpose.text: Support user-requested website traffic, content, audience, engagement, conversion, revenue, real-time and search-performance analysis using GA4 and Search Console, together with URL indexing requests and index-status inspection. Preserve analysis results and produce human-readable summaries. These are conditional toolkit purposes; the source does not establish authorization to execute any particular operation.

evidences.reason: Defines the toolkit's analytics, search-performance and indexing purposes in terms of user requests.
Defines the analysis, result-saving and summary workflow.
Additionally documents URL-removal requests and URL inspection as distinct supported operations.

requirements.text: For toolkit setup, install the dependencies from the scripts directory and use Node.js version 18 or later.

evidences.reason: Explicitly directs dependency installation from the scripts directory.
Declares the required Node.js engine version.

requirements.text: For toolkit configuration, create a project-root .env file containing the GA4 property identifier, service-account email and private key, Search Console site URL, and default date-range configuration. The displayed credential and site values are examples rather than actual task inputs.

evidences.reason: Specifies the configuration file and its environment-variable entries using example values.

requirements.text: For full toolkit setup, provide a Google Cloud project with the Analytics Data API, Search Console API and Indexing API enabled, and a service account with access to the GA4 property and Search Console.

evidences.reason: States the toolkit prerequisites explicitly.

requirements.text: For an analysis selected by the user's request, run the relevant API functions to obtain structured Google API data. The function catalog does not require every available operation to run for each analysis.

evidences.reason: Maps different user requests to different function selections.
Requires API execution as the analysis phase.

requirements.text: Automatically save all analysis results as timestamped JSON files under results/{category}/, using the YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS__operation filename pattern and an extra-information suffix when supplied. Preserve the explicit save=false exception for granular functions that expose it; high-level analyses save their resulting combined output.

evidences.reason: States the automatic saving obligation, destination and filename pattern.
Identifies the report, real-time, Search Console, indexing and summary storage categories.
Documents a configurable save option with a true default for granular reports.
Shows that date comparison suppresses intermediate saves but saves both periods in the combined result.

requirements.text: After analysis, read the saved JSON results and create a Markdown summary in results/summaries/ containing data tables, trends and recommendations.

evidences.reason: Explicitly requires the summary, its input, destination and contents.

requirements.text: For operations that accept date ranges, use the supplied range and support day-count shorthand and explicit startDate/endDate objects. GA4 also supports relative-date objects. Use the configured default range when omitted, with 30d as the default configuration. Convert Search Console shorthand ranges to YYYY-MM-DD dates rather than GA4 relative-date strings.

evidences.reason: Defines date-range formats and the configurable default.
Preserves explicit date objects and maps day-count shorthand to GA4 relative dates.
States Search Console's date-format constraint and converts shorthand to calendar-date strings.

requirements.text: When siteOverview is selected, provide a site snapshot containing page views, traffic sources, demographics and events for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the information gathered by the site overview.

requirements.text: When trafficAnalysis is selected, provide traffic-source data, sessions grouped by source and medium, and a new-versus-returning breakdown. Include sessions, engagedSessions, averageSessionDuration and bounceRate in the source/medium report, and activeUsers, sessions and conversions in the new-versus-returning report.

evidences.reason: Defines the traffic-analysis components.
Specifies the dimensions and metrics of the additional traffic-analysis reports.

requirements.text: When contentPerformance is selected, provide page-view, landing-page and exit-page analysis for the applicable range. Group landing-page sessions, activeUsers, bounceRate and averageSessionDuration by landingPage, and group exits and screenPageViews by pagePath.

evidences.reason: Defines the three content-performance components.
Specifies the landing-page and exit-page report contents.

requirements.text: When userBehavior is selected, provide demographics, events and daily engagement metrics. The daily report groups activeUsers, engagedSessions, engagementRate and averageSessionDuration by date.

evidences.reason: Defines the user-behavior analysis components.
Specifies the daily engagement report alongside demographics and events.

requirements.text: When compareDateRanges is selected, report the same dimensions and metrics for both supplied ranges and retain each range alongside its corresponding period data. Default to the date dimension and activeUsers, sessions and screenPageViews metrics when custom selections are omitted.

evidences.reason: Requires a side-by-side comparison of two date ranges.
Defines defaults, matching report selections and the association between each input range and its returned data.

requirements.text: When liveSnapshot is selected, provide current active-user, currently viewed page and current-event data together in the snapshot.

evidences.reason: Defines the three kinds of real-time snapshot information.
Associates the active-user, page and event results with the combined snapshot.

requirements.text: When a custom runReport operation is selected, require dimensions and metrics, apply the applicable date range and any supplied dimension filters, sort order and row limit, and return rows containing dimension and metric values.

evidences.reason: Defines the custom-report input and output contract, including optional filtering, ordering and row limiting.

requirements.text: When getPageViews is selected, report screenPageViews, activeUsers and averageSessionDuration grouped by pagePath and pageTitle for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the page-view report's dimensions and metrics.

requirements.text: When getTrafficSources is selected, report sessions, activeUsers, newUsers and bounceRate grouped by sessionSource, sessionMedium and sessionCampaignName for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Specifies the traffic-source report's dimensions and metrics.

evidences.reason: Specifies the demographic report's dimensions and metrics.

requirements.text: When getEventCounts is selected, report eventCount, eventCountPerUser and activeUsers grouped by eventName for the applicable date range.

requirements.text: When getRealtimeEvents is selected, return current event counts grouped by eventName.

evidences.reason: Defines the current-event result and its grouping.

requirements.text: When getRealtimePages is selected, return current page-view counts grouped by unifiedScreenName.

evidences.reason: Defines the current-page result and its grouping.

requirements.text: When getRealtimeSources is selected, return current active-user counts grouped by firstUserSource and firstUserMedium.

requirements.text: When searchConsoleOverview is selected, provide top queries, top pages, device performance and country performance for the applicable range.

evidences.reason: Defines the Search Console overview components.

evidences.reason: Describes queries with a device breakdown.

requirements.text: When seoPagePerformance is selected, provide top pages by clicks and a country breakdown for the applicable range, retaining the unresolved conflict about the ranking used by its shared top-pages function.

evidences.reason: Specifies top pages by clicks and a country breakdown.

requirements.text: When querySearchAnalytics is selected, query the configured Search Console site using the selected dimensions, date range, row limit and pagination offset. Default to the query dimension, a row limit of 1000 and an offset of zero. Return rows containing keys, clicks, impressions, ctr and position.

evidences.reason: Defines the query options, defaults, supported dimension examples and response fields.
Associates the query parameters with the configured Search Console site.

evidences.reason: Specifies the query ranking, count limit and date-range applicability.

requirements.text: When getDevicePerformance is selected, return search-performance data broken down by device type for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the device-performance breakdown.

requirements.text: When getCountryPerformance is selected, return search performance by country for the top 50 countries, subject to available results, for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the country breakdown and its count limit.

requirements.text: When getSearchAppearance is selected, return search-appearance performance data for the applicable date range.

evidences.reason: Defines the search-appearance operation and its date-range applicability.

requirements.text: When requestIndexing is selected for a full URL, submit a re-crawl request and return a notification result containing the URL, type URL_UPDATED and notifyTime. This operation requests indexing rather than establishing that indexing succeeded.

evidences.reason: Defines the full-URL input, requested action and notification-result fields.

requirements.text: When requestIndexingBatch is selected, request re-crawling for the supplied URLs sequentially to avoid rate limits and return the array of notification results.

evidences.reason: Explicitly requires sequential processing and an array of notification results.

requirements.text: When removeFromIndex is selected, request removal of the supplied URL from Google's index and return a notification result containing the URL, type URL_DELETED and notifyTime.

evidences.reason: Defines the separate removal operation and its notification-result representation.

requirements.text: When inspectUrl is selected, inspect the supplied URL within the configured Search Console site and return its index-status information, including verdict and coverageState, with lastCrawlTime, mobile-usability information and rich-results information when available.

evidences.reason: Defines the URL-inspection purpose and result information.
Distinguishes required index-status fields from optional crawl, mobile-usability and rich-results fields.

requirements.text: When reindexUrls is selected, process the supplied URLs in order and return a result for each attempted URL. Successful results include submitted status and the notification result; failures include the input URL, failed status and error text. Continue processing later URLs after a per-URL failure.

evidences.reason: Defines ordered per-URL submission, success and failure records, and continuation after caught errors.

requirements.text: When checkIndexStatus is selected, inspect each supplied URL in order and retain its association with the returned status. Set indexed to true exactly when the inspection verdict is PASS. On a per-URL failure, return indexed=false with error information and continue with later URLs.

evidences.reason: Defines per-URL status association, the PASS test, failure representation and continued processing.

requirements.text: When getAvailableDimensions is selected, return all available dimensions for the GA4 property, with dimension metadata including apiName, uiName and description.

evidences.reason: Defines the complete available-dimension listing and metadata fields.

requirements.text: When getAvailableMetrics is selected, return all available metrics for the GA4 property, with metric metadata including apiName, uiName and description.

evidences.reason: Defines the complete available-metric listing and metadata fields.

evidences.reason: Requires full combined metadata for getPropertyMetadata.

evidences.reason: Explicitly specifies trimming, conditional leading-slash addition and trailing-slash preservation, applying normalization independently through an ordered map.

requirements.text: When buildUrlFilter is selected, build a pagePath inclusion filter from the supplied normalized paths using case-insensitive matching. Return null when the supplied path list is empty.

evidences.reason: Defines the pagePath filter, supplied inclusion values, case-sensitivity setting and empty-list result.

requirements.text: When getMetricsForUrls is selected, normalize and filter to the supplied page paths, then return metrics grouped by pagePath and pageTitle for the applicable range. For an empty path list, return rows=[] and rowCount=0 without running a report.

evidences.reason: Defines the bulk-lookup inputs, default metrics and per-URL result purpose.
Defines normalization, empty-input behavior, path filtering and the pagePath/pageTitle grouping.

evidences.reason: Defines loading a saved result and its nullable return.

evidences.reason: Requires category selection, newest-first ordering, optional limiting and file-path results.
Defines the absent-category result and limits the ordered JSON-file listing.

requirements.text: When getLatestResult is selected, return the most recent saved result in the selected category, restricted to the specified operation when provided, or null when no matching result is available.

evidences.reason: Defines category selection, optional operation filtering and a nullable latest-result return.
Specifies null when the filtered result list is empty.
Presents alternative user requests and corresponding operations rather than selecting one.
Catalogs several distinct analytics, search, indexing and metadata purposes.

issues.reason: The frozen source defines a reusable toolkit but supplies no concrete operational user request. Preserve the operation-specific contracts conditionally; do not infer that all operations are required or that any external operation is authorized.

evidences.reason: Describes automatic saving of all results without stating an exception.
Exposes a boolean save option with a true default for a granular report.
Disables intermediate comparison saves and then persists the combined result containing both periods.

issues.reason: Retain automatic saving as the analysis workflow and default behavior. Apply the explicit save option to granular calls that expose it. Date comparison saves both period results within its combined output; the source does not require separate duplicate files for those intermediate calls.

evidences.reason: States that all functions accept flexible date ranges.
Defines real-time functions with save arguments and no date-range argument.
Defines indexing and inspection functions around URL inputs and save options rather than date ranges.

issues.reason: The specific function contracts determine date-range applicability. Retain flexible date ranges for date-aware analytics operations without adding historical range requirements to real-time, indexing or inspection operations.

evidences.reason: Includes GA4 relative-date objects in the generally described supported formats.
Explicitly states that Search Console requires YYYY-MM-DD dates rather than GA4 relative-date strings.

issues.reason: Apply the explicit Search Console format constraint to Search Console operations and retain GA4 relative-date support for GA4 operations. This preserves the narrower API-specific requirement without demanding both incompatible representations for one request.

evidences.reason: Describes the keyword-analysis output as queries with a device breakdown.
Labels device performance as a breakdown for queries while obtaining it separately from the query results.
The device-performance helper groups only by device, without a query dimension.

issues.reason: The description can require device performance associated with individual queries, while the orchestration supplies a separate overall device report. These interpretations require different information relationships. Preserve the source description and the unresolved relationship without inventing a requirement to provide both.

evidences.reason: Defines getTopPages as returning the top 100 pages by search impressions.
Defines SEO page performance using top pages by clicks.
Uses the shared top-pages helper for the clicks-described SEO analysis.
Also directly describes getTopPages as returning top pages by clicks.

issues.reason: The same top-pages operation is described with two different ranking criteria. The supplied material does not establish which criterion governs. Preserve both source-located descriptions without requiring two rankings or silently choosing one.
